- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts often overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history, leading to overcorrection or delayed mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; forecasts fail to adjust downward quickly when true outcomes show strong downward drift.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes in the first 5–7 days, then gradually catch up — suggesting a delay in reacting to recent price changes.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts show exaggerated peaks and troughs compared to actual price behavior.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to overestimate continuation, ignoring potential reversal or consolidation.
- Forecasts are less sensitive to low-value history (e.g., <65) and overreact to high-value history (e.g., >75), leading to inconsistent calibration.
